summary: Source-anchored research for Shard key index design. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: For normal covered queries through mongos on sharded collections, the chosen index must contain the shard key as well as all query and returned fields. Exclude _id from the projection when it is absent from that index. (medium confidence)

Shard-key support and query coverage impose different requirements: a supporting compound index has the shard key as its prefix; query coverage additionally requires the query and projection fields in the same index. The coverage rule itself says the index must contain the shard key, not that every covering index must put it first. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-shard-key-indexes.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

A covering projection must exclude _id explicitly when _id is absent from the chosen index. Returning complete documents, or omitting other returned fields from the index, defeats coverage. (medium confidence)

The 2014 Stack Overflow answer explicitly scopes the inability to obtain fully covered sharded queries to MongoDB 2.6; its January 2015 follow-up says SERVER-5022 was resolved in the 2.7 development cycle. Current documentation permits coverage subject to shard-key inclusion, so the old blanket prohibition must not be applied to current deployments. (medium confidence) Sources: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24952791/cannot-get-a-covered-query-for-sharded-collection-in-mongodb ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

For range-sharded collections, uniqueness constraints generally require the shard key as an index prefix; the default _id index is an exception whose uniqueness is only per shard when _id is not the shard key. Index design must consider uniqueness separately from coverage. (low confidence)

Hashed indexes cannot cover queries. A hashed shard-key index therefore does not itself provide coverage merely because it supports sharding; evaluate a separate non-hashed index containing the raw shard-key fields and the other query/projection fields. (medium confidence)

SERVER-48471 records a historical failure in which concurrent writes during a hashed index build incorrectly marked the index multikey, making shardCollection reject it with "couldn't find valid index for shard key". The issue lists fixes in 4.2.12, 4.4.4, and 4.9.0; this is historical troubleshooting evidence, not an assertion of a current-version defect. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29)

The manual documents an exception to retaining the hashed shard-key index starting in 7.0.3, 6.0.12, and 5.0.22. Dropping it disables balancing for that collection; the procedure recommends a supporting non-hashed index to avoid collection scans for shard-key predicates. This is an operational trade-off, not a prerequisite for coverage. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/drop-a-hashed-shard-key-index.md

Dropping a hashed shard-key index is an operational trade-off: MongoDB recommends a supporting non-hashed index to avoid collection scans for shard-key filters, and excludes that collection from balancing until the hashed index is recreated. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

An index supporting the shard key may be the shard-key index itself or a compound index with the shard key as its prefix. A populated collection needs that supporting index before sh.shardCollection(). (low confidence)

Covering indexes should be sized for actual access patterns. Extra indexes consume storage and increase write maintenance; periodic review should remove unnecessary indexes while retaining required shard-key support. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/want-mongodb-performance-you-will-need-to-add-and-remove-indexes/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-shard-key-indexes.md

Validate routing and local access patterns together. ArchTenet describes an incident where queries omitted the region shard key and lacked workload-specific indexes, causing broadcast collection scans; Percona independently advises identifying query patterns to choose indexes. Sources: https://archtenet.dev/blog/mongodb-geosharding-hidden-cost/ ; https://www.percona.com/blog/want-mongodb-performance-you-will-need-to-add-and-remove-indexes/

For ranged sharding, a unique secondary compound index must have the shard key as a prefix. Uniqueness applies to the full indexed combination, so adding a field for coverage can change which combinations are constrained. (low confidence)

For a range-sharded collection with shard key {tenantId:1}, a proposed index {tenantId:1,status:1,total:1} can both support the shard key and cover find({tenantId:T,status:S},{total:1,_id:0}), assuming scalar values, no null equality, and compatible query/index options. This is a design inference from the documented rules, not a measured plan. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-shard-key-indexes.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

Shard key choice should keep the number of shards contacted per query low, ideally one, because cross-shard queries are expensive. Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/choosing-a-good-sharding-key-in-mongodb-and-mysql/

The 2019 Stack Overflow example has a compound shard key containing app_id, android_id, and another field, while its proposed predicate index omits the latter two fields. Together with the absent restricted projection, this explains why matching predicate fields alone did not establish coverage; the thread does not establish a universal planner-ranking rule. (medium confidence)
MongoDB supports compound hashed shard keys containing one hashed field plus other fields. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/hashed-sharding.md
